title: Alzheimer's Disease
subtitle: The most common form of dementia, a progressive neurological disease that destroys memory and thinking skills. It accounts for 60-80% of all dementia cases.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Alzheimer's affects over 55 million people worldwide. It is the 7th leading cause of death globally. Early diagnosis allows for better planning and access to treatments that can temporarily slow symptoms.
items: Memory loss disrupting daily life, forgetting recently learned information
Difficulty with problem-solving and planning familiar tasks
Confusion with time, dates, seasons, and passage of time
Vision and spatial difficulties, trouble judging distances
Withdrawing from social activities and hobbies
Changes in mood, personality, confusion, suspicion, depression

sections.title: Causes & Risk Factors
sections.intro: Alzheimer's is caused by abnormal protein deposits in the brain that disrupt communication between nerve cells, leading to cell death and brain shrinkage.
items: Amyloid plaques, abnormal clumps of beta-amyloid protein between neurons
Tau tangles, twisted strands of tau protein inside neurons
APOE-e4 gene, major genetic risk factor (3-4x increased risk)
Age is the biggest risk factor, doubles every 5 years after 65
Head injuries and poor cardiovascular health increase risk
Women have higher lifetime risk (partly due to longer lifespan)

sections.title: Prevention & Lifestyle
items: Stay mentally active, learning new skills, reading, puzzles
Regular physical exercise, improves blood flow to brain
Maintain good cardiovascular health, control blood pressure and diabetes
Maintain social connections and engage with community
Mediterranean and MIND diet associated with lower risk
Quality sleep, brain clears amyloid during deep sleep

sections.title: Treatment
items: Cholinesterase inhibitors, Donepezil, Rivastigmine, Galantamine (slow decline)
Memantine, for moderate to severe cases
Lecanemab (Leqembi), new anti-amyloid therapy; slows early-stage decline
Cognitive stimulation therapy and structured routine
Caregiver support and respite care programs
Safe home modifications, fall prevention, wandering alarms

facts: Over 60% of Alzheimer's patients are cared for at home
Memory problems alone are not always Alzheimer's, consult a specialist
